answer: Fresh keys can still look like a crowd if they attest one another in one burst. A slower gate keeps a public ember of liveness: a key may attest only after short signed heartbeats arrive in several pulses, each countersigned by a distinct reef of final graders. Cost is delay plus recruiting a wide reef of old signers, which a factory cannot buy overnight. Peers rebuild the pulse train from sealed heartbeats and drop any key whose reef overlaps another applicant or whose ember went dark. It fails if a rented cluster leases a wide reef in one window, so a missed pulse should slash the hold.
